pages.text: Desmatochelys comes from the Cretaceous, with fossils found across the Northern hemisphere. It is a large protostegid sea turtle, growing up to 2 m in length. Desmatochelys is currently the oldest known sea turtle, with the oldest specimens coming in at 120 million years old. Although unlike modern sea turtles, Desmatochelys may have laid rigid, hard-shelled eggs instead of the standard soft-shelled eggs.

It is also known from multiple complete to near-complete specimens, alongside some partial shell material, which is also distinct from other marine sea turtles. The generic name derives from the Greek words 'desmos', to mean 'link'; and 'khelus', to mean 'tortoise'.
